name: Frontend Design
shortDescription: Guides an agent toward distinctive, opinionated visual design instead of generic templated UI.
whenToHelp: Reach for it when building or reshaping a UI and the output keeps coming out looking like a generic template rather than something with a point of view.
whatItDoes: Frames the agent as a design lead at a studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity. It pushes the agent to ground design decisions in the actual subject matter (industry, audience, content) rather than defaults, make deliberate typography/palette/layout choices, and take justified aesthetic risks instead of falling back to generic boilerplate.
bestThing: It explicitly tells the agent to identify the real subject matter and audience before designing anything, so the output is grounded in the brief instead of generic aesthetic guesses.
author: Anthropic
howToInstall: In Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills, then /plugin install example-skills@anthropic-agent-skills. Already available on claude.ai for paid plans. Plain SKILL.md content with no Claude-specific dependency, so it also works copied directly into Cursor's .cursor/rules/ or Codex's ~/.codex/skills/ — confirmed by existing community ports.
sourceNote: Curated 2026-09-28 from Anthropic's official skills repo.

name: MCP Builder
shortDescription: Step-by-step guide for building high-quality MCP servers that expose external APIs as agent tools.
whenToHelp: Reach for it when integrating a third-party API or internal service into an agent workflow and you want the resulting tool definitions to actually be usable by an LLM, not just technically correct.
whatItDoes: Walks through a four-phase workflow for MCP server development (Python/FastMCP or Node/TypeScript) — planning tool surface area, implementing well-designed tool schemas, and validating that an LLM can actually complete real tasks with the tools, rather than just wrapping an API 1:1.
bestThing: It measures success by "how well it enables LLMs to accomplish real-world tasks," not by API coverage — a genuinely different bar than typical SDK-wrapper generators.
author: Anthropic
howToInstall: In Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills, then install via the plugin UI. Pure guide + reference docs, no Claude-specific runtime dependency, so it also works copied into any harness that reads SKILL.md files (Cursor, Codex).
sourceNote: Curated 2026-09-28 from Anthropic's official skills repo.

name: Web Application Testing
shortDescription: Toolkit for testing and debugging local web apps with Playwright — screenshots, browser logs, functional verification.
whenToHelp: Reach for it after building a local frontend, to verify it actually works in a real browser rather than trusting the code looks right.
whatItDoes: Provides a decision tree (static HTML vs. dynamic app) and a server-lifecycle helper script so the agent can spin up the app, drive it with native Playwright, capture screenshots, and read console/network logs to debug UI behavior — kept as black-box scripts to avoid bloating context.
bestThing: It explicitly instructs the agent not to read the helper script source unless truly necessary, to avoid polluting the context window — an unusually deliberate context-economy design choice.
author: Anthropic
howToInstall: In Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills, then install via the plugin UI. Requires Playwright available in the environment. Plain Python scripts run via bash, no Claude-specific API calls, so it also works in Cursor or Codex agents with bash + Python access.
sourceNote: Curated 2026-09-28 from Anthropic's official skills repo.

name: Humanizer
shortDescription: Rewrites AI-generated text to remove the tells of AI writing while preserving meaning.
whenToHelp: Reach for it whenever output needs to stop reading like an LLM wrote it — before sending an email, publishing a post, or submitting written work.
whatItDoes: Detects and rewrites roughly 26 patterns of AI-sounding prose (em-dash cascades, "it's worth noting that," triadic lists, inflated vocabulary, staged run-ups) based on Wikipedia's "Signs of AI writing" guide, while explicitly preserving factual accuracy and original meaning.
bestThing: It's not a vague style pass — it's built on a named, checkable pattern list (26 specific signs), so the rewriting is auditable rather than a black box.
author: blader
howToInstall: Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add blader/humanizer, then /plugin install humanizer@humanizer. Codex: npx skills add blader/humanizer --global --agent codex. Other agents: npx skills add blader/humanizer --global --agent '*'. Claude.ai/Desktop: download the repo ZIP and upload as a custom skill.
sourceNote: Curated 2026-09-28. Replaces the original phase-1a placeholder entry of the same name, which was an internal, unsourced stand-in for this exact kind of skill.

name: Claude Code Prompt Improver
shortDescription: A hook system that silently improves prompts at submit-time before Claude acts on them.
whenToHelp: Reach for it when prompts tend to be vague and you want sharper first-attempt results without manually rewriting every request.
whatItDoes: Injects context-aware nudges at three points — prompt submit, tool use, and subagent start — covering clarity assessment, workflow-planning guidance, and multi-file approach routing. Nudges fire conditionally rather than on every prompt.
bestThing: It's hook-based rather than skill-based, so it operates automatically on every prompt without the user having to remember to invoke anything.
author: severity1
howToInstall: Marketplace (recommended): add the severity1 marketplace, then install the prompt-improver plugin in Claude Code. Manual: copy the scripts/nudges into ~/.claude/hooks/ and register three hook entries in ~/.claude/settings.json. Requires Claude Code 2.0.22+. Genuinely Claude Code-only — depends on Claude Code's specific hook format and the AskUserQuestion tool, neither of which exist elsewhere.
sourceNote: Curated 2026-09-28. Modifies ~/.claude/settings.json via hooks — verify the actual hook code yourself before installing, this wasn't independently audited beyond reading its README.

name: Superpowers
shortDescription: A full agentic software-development methodology packaged as composable skills — brainstorming through TDD, debugging, and code review.
whenToHelp: Reach for it for general-purpose coding work where you want a disciplined process (spec, plan, TDD implementation, review) rather than ad hoc code generation.
whatItDoes: Chains together skills that activate automatically by task type: brainstorming to refine a rough idea into a spec, design validation, task planning, red-green-refactor TDD implementation, systematic root-cause debugging, and code review/branch finalization — meant to function as a complete SDLC for an agent.
bestThing: Skills trigger automatically based on task type (brainstorming activates for new features, systematic-debugging takes over when something breaks) rather than requiring the user to invoke each stage manually.
author: Jesse Vincent (obra) / Prime Radiant
howToInstall: Claude Code: /plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official. Cursor: /add-plugin superpowers. Devin CLI: devin plugins install obra/superpowers. GitHub Copilot: copilot plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace. Platform-specific commands vary, see the repo README.
sourceNote: Curated 2026-09-28. Value claim (packaged process vs. ad hoc prompting) is plausible but not independently confirmed to outperform the ad hoc version — verify yourself before fully trusting the pitch.

name: Playwright MCP
shortDescription: Official Microsoft MCP server for browser automation via Playwright, using structured accessibility snapshots instead of screenshots.
whenToHelp: Reach for it when an agent needs to actually drive, inspect, or test a real website — filling forms, navigating flows, scanning a page's structure — deterministically rather than guessing from a screenshot.
whatItDoes: Exposes Playwright's browser automation as MCP tools: navigate, click, fill forms, extract structured accessibility-tree snapshots of a page, take screenshots, and run scripted browser interactions — usable for both testing and general web-scanning/agentic-browsing tasks.
bestThing: It uses the accessibility tree as its primary signal rather than screenshots, which makes it fast, deterministic, and usable without a vision-capable model.
author: Microsoft
howToInstall: Not a skill folder — it's an MCP server. Run npx @playwright/mcp@latest, or add to your MCP config JSON: {"mcpServers": {"playwright": {"command": "npx", "args": ["@playwright/mcp@latest"]}}}. Also published on npm as @playwright/mcp; most clients have a one-click or CLI mcp add shortcut.
sourceNote: Curated 2026-09-28. The standalone-tool example for this batch — found via open web search, not any GitHub skill-directory site, since it isn't a SKILL.md file.

name: HashiCorp Agent Skills (Terraform)
shortDescription: HashiCorp's official skill set for Terraform/Packer — scaffolding providers, writing modules, and following house infrastructure-as-code conventions.
whenToHelp: Reach for it when writing or scaffolding Terraform infrastructure code and you want it grounded in HashiCorp's actual conventions instead of the LLM hallucinating provider syntax — a known failure mode for Terraform specifically.
whatItDoes: 20 skills across two product areas (16 Terraform, 4 Packer), covering code generation, module generation, provider development (including scaffolding a brand-new Terraform provider), and policy-as-code patterns.
bestThing: It's maintained directly by HashiCorp itself, not a community reverse-engineering of Terraform conventions, so the guidance traces back to the actual house style rules.
author: HashiCorp
howToInstall: Individual skill: npx skills add hashicorp/agent-skills/plugins/terraform/skills/[skill-name]. Claude Code product bundle: claude plugin marketplace add hashicorp/agent-skills, then claude plugin install terraform@hashicorp.

name: SuperSEO Skills
shortDescription: 11 Claude skills for SEO content work — page audits, article writing, E-E-A-T scoring, link-building strategy, competitor/semantic-gap analysis.
whenToHelp: Reach for it when producing or auditing content meant to rank — a blog post, a landing page, a content strategy — and you want it grounded in named SEO methodology rather than generic "write good content" advice.
whatItDoes: The agent autonomously gathers its own research (search results, competitor pages) rather than requiring the user to paste data in, then runs it through methodology attributed to named practitioners for page audits, article writing, E-E-A-T audits, and link-building, plus a generation-time anti-AI-slop ruleset to keep output from reading like filler.
bestThing: It bakes in an explicit anti-AI-slop ruleset at generation time — a direct, self-aware counter to the exact failure mode SEO content generators are usually criticized for.
author: InhouseSEO
howToInstall: Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add inhouseseo/superseo-skills, then /plugin install superseo@superseo-skills. Manual: clone the repo and copy skill folders into your local skills directory, or paste into any other agent's system prompt — the repo's own README states it contains no executable code and gives an explicit Cursor install path (copy into .cursor/rules/).
sourceNote: Curated 2026-09-28. Value claim (structured methodology vs. ad hoc SEO prompting) is plausible but not independently confirmed to outperform the ad hoc version — verify yourself before fully trusting the pitch.
